newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle expected lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle expected lower.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures, alike, were expected to open 0.100 to 0.200 cent per lb lower, livestock analysts said.

Expectations of further weakness in fed cattle markets the next few weeks will likely weigh on live cattle futures. Although there was active feedlot movement Monday, fed cattle supplies loom large which will keep packer bids down.
Lower boxed beef values will also will weigh on fed cattle bids, analysts said.
Beef movement was good over the holiday weekend but fill-in demand is slack which will keep pressure on the boxed beef market, they added.
Feeder cattle futures are also expected to show pressure despite posting of a new contract high in August and mostly higher closes on Monday, sources said.
The index has turned lower and corn futures indications point higher which should combine to weigh on feeder futures, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was down $0.68 per cwt for the two days ending last Friday to $80.19 per cwt.
